name: pwrite
synopsis: ssize_t pwrite(int fd, const void *buf, size_t count, off_t offset);
description: pwrite() writes up to count bytes from the buffer starting at buf to the file descriptor fd at the specified offset. The file offset is not changed, allowing writes at a specific position without affecting the file pointer. The file must be seekable.

parameters.name: buf
parameters.description: Buffer containing the data to write

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Number of bytes to write from the buffer

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Offset from the beginning of the file where the write should occur

return_value.success: Returns the number of bytes written
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: Any error specified for write(2) or lseek(2), such as EBADF for invalid file descriptor

bugs: On Linux, if a file is opened with O_APPEND, pwrite() appends data to the end of the file regardless of the specified offset, contrary to POSIX requirements.
versions: Added in Linux 2.1.60; glibc support in glibc 2.1
